question:
A 67-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has had lower back pain for several months. The pain radiates down the right leg to the foot. He has no history of any serious illness and takes no medications. His pain increases after activity. The straight leg test is positive on the right. The results of the laboratory studies show:
Laboratory test
Hemoglobin 14 g/d
Leukocyte count 5,500/mm3 with a normal differential
Platelet count 350,000/mm3
Serum
Calcium 9.0 mg/dL
Albumin 3.8 g/dL
Urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL
  Serum immunoelectrophoresis shows an immunoglobulin G (IgG) type monoclonal component of 40 g/L. Bone marrow plasma cells return at 20%. Skeletal survey shows no bone lesions. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) shows a herniated disc at the L5. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Positive straight leg test on the right" -> "Indicates sciatic nerve irritation" -> "Likely due to herniated disc at L5" -> "40 g/L IgG monoclonal component on serum immunoelectrophoresis" -> "Suspicion of multiple myeloma" -> "Next step: Further evaluation for multiple myeloma" -> 80%

enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with lower back pain, positive straight leg test on the right, and the presence of a 40 g/L IgG monoclonal component on serum immunoelectrophoresis raises suspicion for multiple myeloma. The most appropriate next step would be further evaluation for multiple myeloma, which may include consultation with a hematologist/oncologist for appropriate management.
analysis: The patient's presentation with lower back pain, positive straight leg test, and the presence of an IgG monoclonal component on serum immunoelectrophoresis raises suspicion for multiple myeloma. Given the findings of 40 g/L IgG monoclonal component and 20% bone marrow plasma cells, further evaluation for multiple myeloma is warranted. The most appropriate next step would be to consult a hematologist/oncologist for appropriate management.
